notes: §1985:XI.4.4.4 GR7 defines the input procedure's range dynamically (CALL, EXIT, GO TO, PERFORM and declaratives executed from it) and says "The range of the input procedure must not cause the execution of any MERGE, RETURN, or SORT statement", with no stated result; §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR1 lets a SORT be written anywhere outside the declaratives. SortEmitter.EmitSort enters the input phase (CobolSort.EnterProcedure) before the procedure so CobolSort.ReleaseStatement takes a RELEASE executed anywhere in the range; since kb/Work PB5274 GateSortMergeProcedures asks the lexical SORT/MERGE ban only from 2023, and the 85-only GateReleaseReturnRange places RELEASE by the range ProcedureReach.Closure computes (PERFORM, GO TO and ALTER targets followed). Probes at --std 85 (work-rs-02/c5): RELEASE in a PERFORMed paragraph and in a GO TO target outside the section ('R AAA', 'R MMM', 'R ZZZ'); RELEASE reached only through an ALTERed GO TO ('G QQQ'); a USE procedure fired by a failed OPEN (35) in the range RELEASEs ('USE 35', then 'R AAA', 'R DDD', 'R EEE'); (a) an ODO SD record of 3 to 7 characters RELEASEd through a PERFORM; (b) unexecuted SORT and MERGE written in the input procedure compile and run ('R BBB DONE'; COBOL2700/COBOL1572 at --std 2023); a RETURN executed in the input phase through a paragraph shared with an output procedure gives AT END and the sort completes, a result the rule leaves undefined; (c) table SORT COBOL0870. Classes d and f do not reach the input range beyond s8's RETURN INTO TE(K). Witness: RELEASE PERFORMed outside the section (1 ALPHA / 2 BRAVO / 3 CHARL). History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB5274 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5274 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-02.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-02-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: 'The range of the input procedure must not cause the execution of any MERGE, RETURN, or SORT statement', no stated effect, and 1985 SR1 lets a SORT be written anywhere outside declaratives. 2023: §2023:14.9.40.4 GR10 sets 'the EC-SORT-MERGE-ACTIVE exception condition' with undefined results; §2023:14.9.34.4 GR1 sets EC-FLOW-RETURN for a RETURN outside an output procedure; and §2023:14.9.40.3 SR3 / §2023:14.9.24.3 SR1 now refuse at compile time a SORT or MERGE written in an input procedure. So a run-time prohibition became an exception condition, and part of it a compile-time refusal. The range definition (transfers of control, declaratives) is the same.
